# Contract

Generated artifacts that keep the Java IR and TypeScript types in sync.

**Never edit these files by hand.** They are regenerated by the build.

## Contents

| Path | Generated by | Regenerate with |
|---|---|---|
| `schema/plan.schema.json` | `mvn package` in `service/` (exec plugin → `SchemaGeneratorMain`) | `cd service && mvn prepare-package -pl .` |
| `types/plan.d.ts` | npm script in `addin/` | `cd addin && npm run generate-types` |

## Drift detection

CI runs both generation steps on a clean checkout and then checks:

```bash
git diff --exit-code contract/
```

A non-zero exit means a Java record changed without a corresponding type regeneration.
This makes drift a build failure rather than a runtime surprise.

## Why this exists

The IR type checker lives in Java; the evaluator and add-in live in TypeScript.
Java owns the IR — the Java records are the source of truth.
The TypeScript types are derived from them at build time.
See `ARCHITECTURE.md §2` for the full rationale.
